Today: 2026-08-17
Quayside ticketing app - project steering meeting, Brennan Valley Transit Authority, 17 August 2026. Quayside is the project these notes are about (the new mobile ticketing and trip-planning app replacing paper passes). The meeting also took short updates from two other authority projects.

Present: Anil Gupta (project director), Colette Martin (fare policy), Nathaniel Boyd (vendor delivery lead, Faregate Systems), Sun-hee Cho (customer experience), Marta Ruiz (finance).

1. Delivery to date
Nathaniel reported that the trip planner, real-time arrivals and account features are complete and passed user acceptance testing in July. The app's payment integration with the authority's card processor is certified. Accessibility testing with the regional disability council found three issues, all fixed. The app had been planned to go live on October 1, alongside the start of the autumn timetable.

2. Fare engine
This is the open item. The fare engine in the app has to implement the fare structure that the authority's board adopts. In June the board deferred its vote on the new zone-based fares after public hearings drew more than 900 comments, and it has asked staff for a revised proposal but has not set a date for the next vote. Colette explained that until the board adopts a fare structure, there is nothing for Faregate to configure: the zone boundaries, transfer rules and concession discounts are all still undecided, and the authority's legal counsel has said the app may not sell tickets on fares that the board has not adopted. Nathaniel confirmed Faregate cannot build or test the fare engine, the ticket purchase flow or the inspector validation app without the fare tables, and those three pieces are everything that remains. Anil asked whether the app could launch with the current flat fares; Colette said the current fares depend on paper transfers that the app cannot represent, and the board has ruled that option out.

3. Customer experience
Sun-hee presented the onboarding screens and the migration plan for 14,000 monthly paper-pass holders. Riders will get a code in their September pass envelope to claim a digital pass. She asked for a decision on whether to send the codes at all if the app is not available, and the group agreed to hold the mail-out.

4. Finance
Marta said the vendor contract is fixed-price with milestone payments. The next payment is tied to the fare-engine milestone and will not be due until that milestone is accepted. Faregate has agreed to keep its team on the project at no extra cost for now, working on documentation and the operations dashboard.

5. Other authority projects (brief)
- Bus shelter replacement: running a month late because of a steel shortage; new completion date December 15.
- Real-time signage at rail stations: complete at 18 of 22 stations.
- Bike-share partnership: the authority cancelled its tender in July after no bidder met the insurance requirements.

6. Next steps
- Colette: share the revised fare proposal timetable with the steering group as soon as staff have one.
- Anil: brief the board chair on the dependency of Quayside on the fare vote.
- Sun-hee: hold the paper-pass mail-out and prepare rider messaging.
- Nathaniel: complete the operations dashboard and handover documentation.

Next steering meeting: 14 September 2026.

Meridian 智慧行程規劃｜PRD 里程碑（Beta 版）
產品：Meridian（旅行社官網的 AI 行程規劃工具）　PM：Hannah 謝　工程：Leo、Mandy、Ivan
最後更新：2026-09-08。本頁只涵蓋 Meridian，旅行社的訂房系統改版另有文件。

1. 背景
旅行社官網目前只有固定的套裝行程。Meridian 讓旅客輸入天數、預算與偏好，自動排出日本、韓國自由行的每日行程，並可一鍵轉成訂房與交通查詢。Beta 版對外開放日訂在 10/15，配合秋季旅展。

2. 里程碑與實際進度
- M1 景點資料庫（日、韓 2,400 個景點，含營業時間與交通時間矩陣）：原訂 7/31，7/29 完成。
- M2 行程排程引擎（受限最佳化＋LLM 文字說明）：原訂 8/28，9/4 完成。晚了一週，是因為東京地區的交通時間矩陣資料有誤，重新抓取花了 5 天；已修正，並補上資料驗證排程。
- M3 前台介面與訂房串接：原訂 9/25。前台介面完成 70%，訂房 API 串接已在測試區跑通。M2 晚掉的一週，工程團隊用 M3 原本預留的兩週緩衝吸收，評估 M3 仍可在 9/25 前完成，10/1–10/10 封閉測試，10/15 對外開放 Beta 不需調整。

- 行程轉訂房比例 ≥ 6%。

- LLM 產生的景點說明可能寫錯營業時間；已改為只顯示資料庫中的營業時間，LLM 只寫推薦理由。
- 旅展期間流量可能是平日的 8 倍，SRE 已完成 10 倍流量壓測。

5. 不在範圍內
- 歐美地區行程（2027 年再評估）。
- 「行程分享社群」子功能：8 月產品會議決定刪除，不做。

訂房系統改版延到 11 月；Meridian 串接的是現行 API，不受影響。

Today: 2026-09-14
PRD: Marlin click-and-collect lockers - milestone update, 14 September 2026. The Marlin locker programme is the subject of this PRD; other Hartwell Stores initiatives appear only where they touch it.

Summary of intent
Marlin was approved in February to place temperature-controlled pickup lockers in 40 Hartwell supermarkets so online grocery customers can collect orders at any hour. The planned deliverables were: locker hardware in all 40 stores, a pickup flow in the Hartwell app, and staff tooling to load lockers from the back of the store. Original rollout: pilot in 5 stores in October, remaining 35 by end of January 2027.

Customer research
Survey of 3,100 online-grocery customers in April: 41 percent said they would use a locker at least once a month; the most cited reason was collecting after work when stores are busy. Willingness to pay a collection fee was low (under 15 percent), so the business case assumed free collection funded by reduced delivery volume.

Milestones so far
- Hardware vendor selected (Fridgelock), contract signed in May.
- App pickup flow designed and usability-tested in June; build 60 percent complete.
- Staff loading tool prototype tested in two stores in August.
- Site surveys done for 32 of 40 stores.

Programme decision, 8 September
At the quarterly investment review, the Chief Operating Officer presented updated delivery economics: the third-party delivery partner cut its per-order price by 35 percent in August, which removes most of the saving the lockers were meant to produce. The COO put the Marlin programme on hold until finance re-runs the business case with the new delivery price; no lockers may be ordered or installed and no further build work may be charged to the programme until that review reports, and finance has not said when it will. The October pilot cannot start without the hardware order, so it is on hold too. Fridgelock has been told to pause the production slot it had reserved, and the two prototype units stay in the test stores for now.

What we are keeping
The store-level stock-reservation API built for Marlin also helps the rapid-delivery team, so it stays in production. The usability findings from the June tests are being handed to the app team for the curbside-pickup screens.

Other initiatives referenced in earlier versions
- Curbside pickup (owned by the app team) is two weeks late because of a parking-bay sensor issue; it continues independently of Marlin.
- The in-store returns kiosk initiative was cancelled in July and is listed here only because it shared a hardware buyer with Marlin.
- The Hartwell rapid-delivery service is waiting on a licence from one city council before it can launch there.

Financials
Spend to date: 1.9 million of the 6.4 million budget. Fridgelock has agreed to hold its price for 90 days. The unspent budget stays frozen inside the programme while the review runs.

People
Product manager Isabel Moreau is helping the curbside-pickup team while the review runs. The two app engineers on the pickup flow are lent to the loyalty squad from October 1. Hardware lead Dmitri Volkov looks after the prototype units.

Document history
v1 Feb 12 (approval), v2 May 20 (vendor), v3 Aug 15 (site surveys), v4 Sep 14 (this edition). Questions to Isabel Moreau.
